evidence: All checks below were run by me on the frozen bytes (read-only; no files written in the workspace other than this report). (1) TOML: Python 3 tomllib parses task.toml (keys schema_version, artifacts, task, metadata, agent, environment, verifier), tests/scoring.toml (gates, weights, floors) and all five judge.toml files (each: judge, scoring, criterion). Criterion counts 1 render / 2 constraints / 43 functional / 6 polish / 3 visual; no duplicate ids in any file; every criterion has the same key set (description, id, name, type, weight; visual adds points = 5 with type = "likert"). Each judge.toml names prompt_template = "prompt.md", that file exists beside it, and each prompt carries only the {app_context} and {criteria} placeholders that tests/test.sh:195-201 and rewardkit resolve; tests/app_context.md exists. (2) Shell: `bash -n` exits 0 for solution/solve.sh and tests/test.sh; both start `#!/bin/bash`; a byte scan of every one of the 43 task files found zero CR bytes, no BOM, valid UTF-8 and a trailing newline in each. (3) Template control: tests/test.sh, tests/Dockerfile, tests/.dockerignore, tests/scoring.toml, tests/tools/score.py, tests/tools/restart_mcp.py and environment/Dockerfile are byte-identical (cmp) to the frozen template; task.toml differs from the template only in the CHANGE_ME identity/metadata lines 5-7, 10-12, 14-15. Both Python tools parse with ast.parse. (4) Seed and reference entry: environment/assets/seed_data.json, solution/app/package.json and package-lock.json parse as JSON; `node --check solution/app/server.js` exits 0 (Node 24 locally); server.js requires only node:path, node:fs, express and better-sqlite3, the two packages both Dockerfiles install globally at the same pinned versions and expose through NODE_PATH, so the copy-only solve.sh needs no install step. server.js:8 reads `process.env.DB_PATH`, server.js:142 listens on `Number(process.env.PORT || 3000)` on 0.0.0.0, serves /api/health and `express.static(path.join(root, 'public'))`, which matches what test.sh launches and probes (test.sh:97-111, 48). The shipped bundle solution/app/public/assets/index.js parses as an ES module (`node --check --input-type=module`), has no top-level import/require left unresolved, and public/index.html references exactly /assets/index.js and /assets/index.css, both present. (5) Run evidence: all 22 artifact hashes in raw-evidence-index.json verify (16 scripted-golden files on raw bytes, 6 hosted-run JSON files on LF-normalised bytes as the index states). `diff -rq` shows the frozen task is byte-identical to projects/colderwater-playground-devtools, the tree run_golden.sh mounts, so the scripted golden did exercise these bytes: it installs with the task's own solve.sh in the agent image, launches with uid 65534, env -i, DB_PATH, NODE_PATH and cwd outside /app, and every recorded result is true with pageErrors [] (runtime 15, editor suite, polish 7, persist-before 8, persist-after 1, restart.json shows revision 2 with history [2, 1] surviving a real process replacement). Counterexample search: I looked for a file that parses locally but would break in the container (CRLF shebang, BOM in TOML, a server-side require outside the global packages, a bundle referencing an absent asset, a prompt placeholder nothing fills, a judge.toml pointing at a missing prompt) and found none. NOTES, not defects: (a) no configured-judge or tests/test.sh run exists for these exact bytes; the hosted run (Oracle 0.9833) was on an earlier candidate (ZIP eda58464, QC input 4f93c627) and is only indirect evidence that the identical test.sh/Dockerfiles launch and grade. (b) The scripted golden ran in the agent image, not the verifier image. (c) My Node syntax check used local Node 24, not the image's Node 22; the scripted golden covers actual execution in the image. (d) I did not recompute the input SHA256 because the manifest hashing recipe is not part of this row's sources. (e) solve.sh is task-specific (not the two-line template): its embedded Node heredoc scans /proc to refuse reinstalling over an open database; it parses and ran in the scripted golden, and whether it satisfies the solve contract belongs to the deterministic check-solve-contract row, not this one.
